IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-0423 created · severity=P1 · source=hosted-api · region=us-west-2 · link=https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-0423
Miriam: early shift here, I'll take primary for the next 4h. Ashwin can you be secondary? Kai if you're around pls ack for follow-up after 09:30 PT. :wave:
Ashwin: ack, I'm secondary. I'll be on-call for escalations and looking at autoscaler behavior.
Miriam: quick summary from paging: increased p95 latency for text-generation routes, some 500s on model-host-03 in us-west-2. User-facing impact = interpolation errors and slow responses for ~6% of requests. SLO alert triggered at 5%.
Miriam: runbooks to check first (ordered):
- Runbook: model-serving-degradation -> https://playbooks.redwood/internal/runbooks/model-serving-degradation
- Cache/KV thrash play -> https://playbooks.redwood/internal/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash
- Traffic routing fallback -> https://playbooks.redwood/internal/runbooks/fallback-routing

Miriam: immediate quick pointers (do these in parallel):
1) Check host metrics for model-host-03 (cpu/gpu mem, oom, nvlink).
   kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide | grep model-host-03
   kubectl -n redwood logs model-host-03 -c runtime --since=10m
2) Check queue/backlog in serving-router dashboard (grafana link) and controller autoscale events.
3) If KV cache thrash suspected, hit admin flush for the prefix for that customer set (ask product for exact prefix if needed):
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://admin.redwood.internal/cache/flush?prefix=kv-cli:12345
4) If errors are 500s from CUDA OOM, kill/restart best-effort on model-host-03 (cordon first if draining):
   kubectl -n redwood drain model-host-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data || true
   kubectl -n redwood delete pod model-host-03

Ashwin: noted. I'm seeing a spike in model runtime GC and repeated small allocations in the logs, might be a memory leak in runtime v2.14. Going to escalate to eng-runtime if restarts don't clear it. Pinged @eng-runtime on the bridge.
Kai: I'm remote but can jump in if needed. I've got the fallback routing recipe open — if we shift 10% traffic to model-v2-quant it should buy us headroom.
Miriam: good. Steps for safe partial fallback:
- Update routing policy in console -> route "text-gen-prod" add fallback model-v2-quant weight=0.1
- Monitor error rate and latency for 2min windows, roll back if errors climb or quality regressions detected.
- CLI snippet to change weights quickly:
  rwctl routes update text-gen-prod --fallback model-v2-quant --weight 0.1

Miriam: customer impact note: at present degraded performance for retail and search customers in us-west-2 only. No billing issues yet. Recommend we open a short status post if we keep >5% degraded for >30m.
Ashwin: I'm seeing 502s with stack trace referencing kv-cache timeouts. I'll run the prefix flush now and keep an eye.
Ashwin: ran flush, waiting 60s to observe. Also increasing per-connection timeout on the router from 60s -> 90s as emergency buffering, will revert after triage.
Miriam: doing controlled restart of model-host-03 now (will drain first). I'll leave note in the incident timeline.
IncidentBot: Timeline event added: Miriam drained and restarted model-host-03 at 1768423260.
Kai: after restart, p95 dropped ~22% but still above SLO. I'm going to nudge routing to shift 15% to model-v2-quant as a safe buffer.
Miriam: agreed, do it for 10-15% and monitor. Also, quick check: APAC overnight coverage gap flagged in the rota — we have no warm pool there; if this becomes multi-region we won't have immediate failover. Logging as action item for infra after incident.
Ashwin: latency improving after cache flush + routing tweak. Error rate down to 0.8% from 3.1%. Good sign.
Miriam: next steps / handoff plan:
- Miriam primary until 12:00Z (1768432000) then Ashwin primary. Kai will be on-call for follow-up and infra coordination.
- Action items: add warm pool for apac (infra), run deeper heap analysis on runtime v2.14 (eng-runtime), create post-incident eval to test quality of model-v2-quant under fallback (ml-evals).
- If SLO remains >5% for next 30m, prepare public status message and notify support.
Kai: ack. I'll create the follow-up infra ticket and pre-populate the incident with logs and command runbook snippets.
Miriam: thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated; escalate to exec page if we can't get under SLO by +45m. :thumbsup:
